intended_object: The orthogonal quotient of a finite symmetric bilinear (Q/Z-valued) module A by a subgroup H: the group H⊥/(H ∩ H⊥) with the pairing induced from A. When H is isotropic this is the classical H⊥/H. Inferred from the docstring and name.
explanation: The definition restricts the pairing of A to H⊥ (`restrict`, with `orthogonalComplement H` = {x | ∀ y ∈ H, b(x,y)=0}). It then takes the quotient by H ∩ H⊥, which appears as `H.addSubgroupOf H⊥`, through `quotientOfLeRadical`. That construction takes the `Submodule` quotient of the ℤ-module and descends the pairing with `liftQ₂`, so the classes satisfy b̄([x],[y]) = b(x,y). The side condition holds: H ∩ H⊥ lies in the radical of the pairing restricted to H⊥, because every element of H pairs to zero with all of H⊥. The result is the standard H⊥/(H∩H⊥) with its induced pairing. For isotropic H (H ≤ H⊥) this is exactly H⊥/H, as the docstring says. Degenerate cases also work: H = 0 gives A, and H = A gives rad(A)/rad(A) = 0. Mathlib has no notion of a finite bilinear module (a finite abelian group with a symmetric ℚ/ℤ-valued pairing), so there is no more general counterpart. The setting is the library's own structure, and the construction is stated at that natural generality.
